title: Global operator and fibres of the Weil $!$-pushforward
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$, with $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite and $n\geq1$, of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated morphism of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $f:X\to Y$ be its geometric base change, and let $\Phi_X,\Phi_Y$ be the $q$-power scheme Frobenii of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Use the comparisons $\theta_{f,m}$ and the Weil $!$-pushforward of [def-trf-weil-shriek-pushforward]. Let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, let $u:L\Phi_X^*K\to K$ be a Frobenius
coefficient morphism of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] (no
invertibility assumed), and let $(L,\psi)=(Rf_!K,Rf_!u\circ\theta_{f,1})$
be its Weil $!$-pushforward, with iterates
$\psi_m=Rf_!u_m\circ\theta_{f,m}$ ([lem-trf-weil-shriek-iterates]).

1. *Global operators.* Let
$c_f:R\Gamma_c(Y,Rf_!K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ be the
composition isomorphism for $a_Yf=a_X$ ([prop-functor-package],
clause (3)). For every $m\geq1$ the global operators of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] satisfy
$$
c_f\circ F_{c,m}(\psi)=F_{c,m}(u)\circ c_f .
$$
1. *Fibres.* Let $m\geq1$, $y\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, and let
$\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ be the geometric point over $y$, so
that $\Phi_Y^m\bar y=\bar y$. Put $X_{\bar y}=X\times_{f,Y,\bar y}\operatorname{Spec}k$,
with $i_{\bar y}:X_{\bar y}\to X$, and $K|_{\bar y}=Li_{\bar y}^*K$.
Then $X_{\bar y}=X_{0,y}\times_{\mathbf F_{q^m}}k$ for the separated
finite-type $\mathbf F_{q^m}$-scheme $X_{0,y}=X_0\times_{Y_0,y}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^m}$,
and for the finite-field datum with $q$ replaced by $q^m$
([def-weil-finite-field-fiber]) the $q^m$-power scheme Frobenius of
$X_{0,y}$ is the restriction $\Phi_{X_{\bar y}}$ of $\Phi_X^m$. The
composite
$$u_m|_{\bar y}:L\Phi_{X_{\bar y}}^*K|_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Li_{\bar y}^*L\Phi_X^{m*}K\xrightarrow{\ Li_{\bar y}^*u_m\ }K|_{\bar y}
$$
is a Frobenius coefficient morphism for this datum, and the proper
base-change isomorphism
$\beta_{\bar y}:L_{\bar y}=\bar y^*Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar y},K|_{\bar y})$
([prop-functor-package], clause (4)) satisfies
$$
\beta_{\bar y}\circ\psi_{m,\bar y}=F_{c,1}\bigl(u_m|_{\bar y}\bigr)\circ\beta_{\bar y},
$$
where $\psi_{m,\bar y}:L_{\bar y}\cong(L\Phi_Y^{m*}L)_{\bar y}\to L_{\bar y}$
is the stalk map of $\psi_m$ at the fixed point $\bar y$ and $F_{c,1}$ is
the degree-one global operator over $\mathbf F_{q^m}$.
1. *Points and stalks.* $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ is the disjoint union of
the sets $X_{0,y}(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ over $y\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, and
for $x\in X_{0,y}(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ with geometric point $\bar x$ the
stalk map of $u_m|_{\bar y}$ at $\bar x$ is the stalk map $u_{m,\bar x}$.

Invertibility of $u$ is used nowhere.

proof.text:
We work only at the finite coefficient stage $A=A_{E,n}$ of the hypothesis. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], bounded constructible inputs have etale-origin witnesses; thus the finite pro-etale domains specified by [fix-lem-exchanges] apply. The map $f_0$ is of finite type by [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target], applied to $X_0\to Y_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$: the source is finite type and the target is separated over $k_0$. All schemes and arrows below are separated of finite type over $k$, and [prop-functor-package] gives the constructible finite-Tor domains. For a finite $h:T'\to T$ set
$$h^\sharp_M=c_h\circ R\Gamma_c(T,\eta_{h,M}):R\Gamma_c(T,M)\to R\Gamma_c(T',Lh^*M),$$
where $c_h$ uses $Rh_*=Rh_!$ and compact-support composition from [prop-functor-package]. The unit and its adjunction are supplied by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. By [prop-trf-graph-operator] and the definition [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism],
$$F_{c,m}(u)=R\Gamma_c(X,u_m)(\Phi_X^m)^\sharp_K,\qquad F_{c,m}(\psi)=R\Gamma_c(Y,\psi_m)(\Phi_Y^m)^\sharp_L.$$
The scheme Frobenii constructed in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius] are finite by [lem-trf-scheme-frobenius-finite-radicial], applied separately to the finite-type models $X_0$ and $Y_0$. For $m=1$ this gives finiteness of $\Phi^m$; for $m+1$, compose the finite maps $\Phi^m$ and $\Phi$ using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. The properness of each ordinary graph leg $\Phi^m$ is also stated explicitly in [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism]. Thus the graph-operator properness hypotheses hold.

source.place: Opening paragraph: definition of the sharp map and graph-operator formulas

proof.text:
For finite $h:T'\to T$ and $h':T''\to T'$, the ordinary composition normalization of [fix-prop-adjunctions], clause (3), gives
$$\eta_{hh'}=(Rh_*\eta_{h'}Lh^*)\circ\eta_h.$$
Use the natural pullback-composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Applying $R\Gamma_c$ to this equation and then the associative compact-support composition isomorphisms of [prop-functor-package], clause (3), gives
$$(hh')^\sharp_M=h'^\sharp_{Lh^*M}\circ h^\sharp_M.$$
This is (α), with all source and target identifications supplied by those same natural composition isomorphisms.

For the Cartesian square defining $X'_m$ in [d-relative-frob], apply [lem-trf-finite-horizontal-shriek-mate] with $g=\Phi_Y^m$, $p=p_m$, $f'=f'_m$. The arrow $g$ is the iterate of the scheme Frobenius constructed in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Its degree-one map is finite by [lem-trf-scheme-frobenius-finite-radicial] applied to $Y_0$, and the induction of Step 1 using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] makes $g$ finite for every $m\geq1$. The finite-horizontal mate lemma then also gives finiteness of $p_m$. Its stated unit equation, after $R\Gamma_c(Y,-)$ and the associative composition identifications of [prop-functor-package], is precisely
$$c_{f'_m}\circ R\Gamma_c(Y,\operatorname{Ex}_!)\circ(\Phi_Y^m)^\sharp_L=(p_m)^\sharp_K\circ c_f.$$
Here $c_{f'_m}$ on the left is evaluated at $Lp_m^*K$, and the occurrence of $c_f$ on the right is evaluated at $K$. This establishes (β) for the actual compact-support exchange, rather than for an unrelated square mate.

Unfold $\theta_{f,m}$ by [def-trf-weil-shriek-pushforward]. The finite map $r_m$ of [i-relative-frob] supplies its middle unit. Under compact-support composition [prop-functor-package], this middle unit followed by the last identification becomes $(r_m)^\sharp_{Lp_m^*K}$. Equations (β) and (α) therefore give
$$c_f\circ R\Gamma_c(Y,\theta_{f,m})\circ(\Phi_Y^m)^\sharp_L=(r_m)^\sharp_{Lp_m^*K}\circ(p_m)^\sharp_K\circ c_f=(\Phi_X^m)^\sharp_K\circ c_f,$$
since $p_mr_m=\Phi_X^m$ by [d-relative-frob]. The iterate identity [lem-trf-weil-shriek-iterates] gives $\psi_m=Rf_!u_m\circ\theta_{f,m}$. Naturality of $c_f$ at $u_m$ and the graph formulas of Step 1 now yield
$$c_f F_{c,m}(\psi)=R\Gamma_c(X,u_m)(\Phi_X^m)^\sharp_K c_f=F_{c,m}(u)c_f.$$
Every operation applied to $u_m$ is functorial; it need not be an isomorphism.

Put $Q=q^m$. By the fibre-product universal property, $X_{\bar y}$ and $X_{0,y}\times_{\mathbf F_Q}k$ are canonically the same $k$-scheme: both are $X_0\times_{Y_0}\operatorname{Spec}k$ for the given rational point. The separated finite-type property of $X_{0,y}\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_Q$ follows from [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] applied to $f_0$. In the affine coordinates of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], a rational point has values in $\mathbf F_Q$, where $z^Q=z$, so $\Phi_Y^m\bar y=\bar y$ as $k$-morphisms. The naturality and factorization equations of [d-relative-frob] then restrict $\Phi_X^m$ to the fibre; its formula on the model coefficients is $a\mapsto a^Q$ and it is identity on $k$. Thus it is exactly the scheme Frobenius of the $\mathbf F_Q$-model $X_{0,y}$. Natural pullback composition [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identifies its pullback on $Li_{\bar y}^*K$ with $Li_{\bar y}^*L\Phi_X^{m*}K$. Pullback preserves the stated coefficient domain by [prop-functor-package], so pulling back $u_m$ gives a morphism of the shape required by [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism].

source.place: (2), first paragraph: fibre model and restricted Frobenius

proof.text:
Write $j':(X'_m)_{\bar y}\to X'_m$ and $i:X_{\bar y}\to X$. Pulling the relative-Frobenius square [d-relative-frob] back along $\bar y$ identifies $(X'_m)_{\bar y}$ with $X_{\bar y}$ and $p_mj'$ with $i$. The base change $s$ of $r_m$ is the endomorphism $\Phi_{X_{\bar y}}$, since $f'_mr_m=f$ and $p_mr_m=\Phi_X^m$. Use the pasting law of [fix-lem-exchanges], clause (2), and compact-support base change [prop-functor-package], clause (4): $\bar y^*\operatorname{Ex}_!$ followed by base change for $f'_m$ equals base change for $f$ along $\Phi_Y^m\bar y=\bar y$.
For the unit in $\theta_{f,m}$ we need the following explicit calculation. Set $A=Lj'^*$, $B=Li^*$ and let $\kappa:Ls^*A\cong B Lr_m^*$ be the pullback square comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. The exchange $E:A Rr_{m*}\to Rs_*B$ of [def-exchange-projection] has components
$$E_N=Rs_*B(\varepsilon_{r_m,N})\circ Rs_*(\kappa_{Rr_{m*}N})\circ\eta_{s,A Rr_{m*}N}.$$
Naturality of $\eta_s$ and $\kappa$ gives, at $N=Lr_m^*M$,
$$E_{Lr_m^*M}\circ A(\eta_{r_m,M})=Rs_*\bigl(B(\varepsilon_{r_m,Lr_m^*M}\circ Lr_m^*\eta_{r_m,M})\bigr)\circ Rs_*(\kappa_M)\circ\eta_{s,AM}=Rs_*(\kappa_M)\circ\eta_{s,AM}.$$
The last equality is the ordinary triangle identity in [fix-prop-adjunctions], clause (1). By [i-relative-frob], $r_m$ is finite and hence proper, so $E$ is the proper-base-change comparison from [prop-functor-package]. Consequently the base change of the middle unit of $\theta_{f,m}$ is exactly the unit of $s$, after $\kappa$. The definition [def-trf-weil-shriek-pushforward] and coherent composition [fix-lem-exchanges] therefore identify, with the coefficient pullback comparisons inserted,
$$\beta_{\bar y}\circ\bar y^*\theta_{f,m}=(\Phi_{X_{\bar y}})^\sharp_{K|_{\bar y}}\circ\beta_{\bar y}.$$
The two occurrences of $\beta_{\bar y}$ have respectively the pulled-back coefficient and original coefficient inputs prescribed by the displayed maps.

source.place: (2), second paragraph: pasting and the explicit proper-exchange unit calculation

proof.text:
By [lem-trf-weil-shriek-iterates], pulling back $\psi_m$ gives $\psi_{m,\bar y}=\bar y^*Rf_!u_m\circ\bar y^*\theta_{f,m}$ under $\bar y^*L\Phi_Y^{m*}=\bar y^*$. Naturality of the compact-support base-change map [fix-lem-exchanges], clause (1), gives
$$\beta_{\bar y}\circ\bar y^*Rf_!u_m=R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar y},u_m|_{\bar y})\circ\beta_{\bar y}$$
with the appropriate coefficient input in each occurrence of $\beta$. Combining this with Step 6 identifies $\beta_{\bar y}\psi_{m,\bar y}$ with
$$R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar y},u_m|_{\bar y})\circ(\Phi_{X_{\bar y}})^\sharp_{K|_{\bar y}}\circ\beta_{\bar y}.$$
By [prop-trf-graph-operator], the first two factors are $F_{c,1}(u_m|_{\bar y})$ for the finite-field datum of Step 5. This proves the fibre identity without using invertibility of $u$.

An $\mathbf F_{q^m}$-point $x$ of $X_0$ determines the unique point $y=f_0x$ of $Y_0$ and, by the fibre-product universal property, an $\mathbf F_{q^m}$-point of $X_{0,y}$. Conversely such a fibre point composes to $x$; these operations are inverse, so the union is disjoint. For stalks write $\bar x_{\mathrm{fib}}:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X_{\bar y}$ and $\bar x=i_{\bar y}\bar x_{\mathrm{fib}}$. Writing derived stalks as pullback along the geometric point, the natural composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] gives
$$L\bar x_{\mathrm{fib}}^*Li_{\bar y}^*M\cong L\bar x^*M.$$
Apply its naturality to $M=L\Phi_X^{m*}K\xrightarrow{u_m}K$, using the commuting fibre/Frobenius square in Step 5. The stalk of the defined composite $u_m|_{\bar y}$ is therefore precisely $u_{m,\bar x}$ under the canonical source and target identifications.
